score_guide.0: Unacceptable: verified fundamental failure, contradiction, or absence of a mandatory control (overrides partial anchors).
score_guide.1: Weak: minimal evidence with substantial deficiencies remaining.
score_guide.2: Partial: core mechanism present, but meaningful gaps remain.
score_guide.3: Baseline: all essential dimension-specific criteria demonstrated by valid, version-bound evidence.
score_guide.4: Robust: baseline plus demonstrable resilience, adversarial coverage, or stronger independent assurance.

dimensions.name: Problem, outcomes, and scope
dimensions.criterion: Assess measurable success metrics (or preapproved justified qualitative criteria), accountable owner, explicit in/out scope, and alternative trade-offs.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite the problem statement, success metrics or justified criterion, scope boundaries, and owner approval.

dimensions.name: Behavioral requirements and acceptance criteria
dimensions.criterion: Assess unambiguous testable acceptance criteria covering success, failure, boundary, authorization, and state-transition invariants.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite versioned functional specs, Given/When/Then cases, and behavior or state-transition contracts.

dimensions.name: Nonfunctional, data, and compatibility requirements
dimensions.criterion: Assess measurable latency, capacity, availability, freshness, consistency, retention, backward-compatibility, and cost bounds with workload assumptions.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite NFR specs, SLI/SLO definitions, workload and cost profiles, and schema or compatibility contracts.

dimensions.name: Technical feasibility and dependencies
dimensions.criterion: Assess feasible component boundaries, API contracts, external dependencies, validation owners, and migration or backfill plans where stateful changes apply.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite ADRs, dependency matrices, API contracts, migration plans, and spike notes.

dimensions.name: Security, privacy, and safety
dimensions.criterion: Assess threat model, trust boundaries, authorization matrix, data classification, privacy obligations, and abuse mitigations.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite threat models or T1 risk checklists, privacy assessments, authorization matrices, and security criteria.

dimensions.name: Traceability and change control
dimensions.criterion: Assess versioned requirement IDs, priorities, owners, acceptance mappings, and change-impact procedures.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite requirement registries, traceability matrices, decision logs, and change policies.

dimensions.name: Delivery, cost, and operational constraints
dimensions.criterion: Assess rollout, rollback or forward-recovery, observability, support ownership, and operational acceptance criteria.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite rollout plans, RTO/RPO targets, ownership matrices, and observability specifications.

critical_conditions.description: An essential behavior has mutually incompatible required outcomes making correct implementation impossible.
A privileged, irreversible, or sensitive-data operation is specified without a bounded authority model.
The specification explicitly violates a mandatory security, privacy, or legal constraint.
A known critical dependency is infeasible and no accepted alternative exists.

dimensions.name: Requirement conformance and scope integrity
dimensions.criterion: Assess whether all essential behaviors are implemented within approved scope with traceable mappings and compatible interfaces.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite clean VCS diffs, requirement-to-code mappings, interface definitions, and review records.

dimensions.name: Architecture, maintainability, and diagnostics
dimensions.criterion: Assess proportionate responsibilities, explicit contracts, bounded dependencies, and structured logs/metrics/traces with PII/secret redaction.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite source trees, ADRs, static analysis, and observability or log-redaction checks.

dimensions.name: Correctness and failure handling
dimensions.criterion: Assess idempotency, consistency, timeouts, retry budgets, concurrency, and explicit error-handling invariants without silent swallowing.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite code paths, unit tests, fault-handling tests, and state-transition evidence.

dimensions.name: Security, privacy, and dependency integrity
dimensions.criterion: Assess enforced authentication/authorization, input validation, secret management, least privilege, and dependency/license integrity.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite security reviews, triaged SAST/SCA output, authorization tests, and dependency manifests.

dimensions.name: Engineering tests, anti-suppression, and build repeatability
dimensions.criterion: Assess clean repeatable builds, passing required CI, reliable unit/component tests, and absence of unauthorized skipped tests or suppressed checks.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite commit SHAs, CI logs, build manifests, unit/component results, and suppression audits.

dimensions.name: Deployment, migration, and recovery
dimensions.criterion: Assess controlled rollout, compatible migrations, and tested non-production rollback or approved forward-recovery containment (exemptible for stateless libraries).
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite deployment specs, migration scripts, compatibility checks, and recovery test logs.

dimensions.name: Reviewability and engineering handoff
dimensions.criterion: Assess recorded scope, accountable ownership, risk-qualified independent review, operating assumptions, and handoff clarity.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite pull requests, independent review records, commit histories, and technical documentation.

critical_conditions.description: Confirmed critical requirement violation in the implemented code.
Reproducible critical data-loss, integrity, or unsafe side-effect defect.
Confirmed unmitigated critical security vulnerability, permission bypass, or production-secret exposure.
Required build or release CI fails for the evaluated source revision.
Unprotected irreversible migration or deployment operation present in a high-impact production path.
Deliberate test/lint suppression or silent failure masking bypassing required engineering checks.

dimensions.name: Requirement coverage and oracle validity
dimensions.criterion: Assess whether every critical acceptance criterion maps to executed tests with independently defensible expected outcomes.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite requirement-test trace matrices, independent test specs, and expected-vs-actual outputs.

dimensions.name: Functional, integration, and compatibility correctness
dimensions.criterion: Assess critical end-to-end, negative, authorization, backward-compatibility, and recovery execution against the release candidate.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite E2E logs, integration test results, failure-case logs, and compatibility reports.

dimensions.name: Performance, resilience, and data quality
dimensions.criterion: Assess applicable mandatory NFRs and data-consistency invariants under representative workloads and stated test limits.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite load/soak reports, chaos or failure tests, workload fixtures, and data reconciliation logs.

dimensions.name: Security and abuse resistance
dimensions.criterion: Assess threat-model-driven authentication, authorization, privacy, and misuse testing with triaged/remediated findings.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite triaged DAST/SAST/SCA findings, authorization tests, abuse-case results, and independent security reviews.

dimensions.name: Test independence and reliability
dimensions.criterion: Assess risk-appropriate oracle independence, isolated execution, repeatable outcomes, and absence of retry-until-green masking.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite test/oracle ownership records, execution metadata, repeated-run stability logs, and flake audits.

dimensions.name: Artifact provenance and config parity
dimensions.criterion: Assess exact release candidate artifact digest binding alongside environment, feature-flag, and migration parity.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite commit/build IDs, artifact digests, environment/config manifests, and parity assessments.

dimensions.name: Defect disposition, operability preflight, and sign-off
dimensions.criterion: Assess authorized defect dispositions, time-bound exceptions, verified rollback and alert-routing preflight, and release sign-off.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite defect registers, retest evidence, exception logs, preflight records, and release approvals.

critical_conditions.description: A critical acceptance test executes and fails against the release candidate.
A confirmed release-blocking security or privacy defect remains unresolved.
A mandatory critical performance, reliability, or data-integrity constraint is violated.
Verification ran against a mismatched build artifact or incompatible configuration/migration state.
Confirmed evidence fabrication, test manipulation, unauthorized suppression, or uninvestigated retry-until-green masking.

dimensions.name: Production reliability, SLOs, and DORA health
dimensions.criterion: Assess approved SLIs, SLO attainment, error-budget adherence, change-failure rate, and MTTR over representative production exposure.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite SLI/SLO reports, error-budget burn logs, DORA metrics, and exposure counts.

dimensions.name: Observability and alert effectiveness
dimensions.criterion: Assess user-impact telemetry coverage, actionable alert routing, and exercised synthetic or drill detection paths.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite metrics, traces, structured logs, dashboards, alert rules, and notification drill records.

dimensions.name: Incident response and recovery
dimensions.criterion: Assess on-call ownership, escalation, runbooks, and RTO/RPO attainment validated via real incidents or controlled game-day drills.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite on-call schedules, incident timelines, game-day logs, runbooks, postmortems, and RTO/RPO measurements.

dimensions.name: Deployment safety, config parity, and disaster recovery
dimensions.criterion: Assess controlled rollouts, config-drift detection, rollback or forward recovery, and backup restoration against objectives.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite deployment logs, drift alerts, rollback/forward-recovery records, and backup-restore or DR drill logs.

dimensions.name: Continuous security, patching, and compliance
dimensions.criterion: Assess vulnerability remediation SLAs, periodic access reviews, tamper-evident audit logging, secret rotation, and retention policies.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite security alerts, access-review logs, CVE SLA trackers, secret-rotation logs, and audit evidence.

dimensions.name: Capacity, cost, and degradation control
dimensions.criterion: Assess capacity headroom, demand-adjusted cost thresholds, forecasts, and load-shedding or graceful degradation controls.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite resource telemetry, capacity forecasts, cost reports, and autoscaling or load-shedding logs.

dimensions.name: Learning, corrective closure, and recurrence
dimensions.criterion: Assess assigned corrective actions with proportionate due dates, verified closure, and recurrence trend monitoring.
dimensions.required_evidence: Cite postmortem registers, corrective-action closure evidence, ownership mappings, and trend analyses.

critical_conditions.description: A confirmed critical service, safety, or security incident remains uncontained beyond mandatory response conditions.
A required critical recovery mechanism is demonstrated to be ineffective.
A material data-integrity or privacy violation continues without containment.
A production rollout or change violates a mandatory error-budget freeze or active safety control.
Operational evidence or telemetry is knowingly manipulated to conceal an incident, SLO breach, or compliance violation.
